title: Bust of Nefertiti

source.author: Rijksmuseum van Oudheden, Leiden (Sketchfab)
source.notes: The Leiden museum's scan of its cast, 4.5 million triangles, one 8192 px texture, in millimetres, with its square base. Raised 1.1 m so the face meets the eye; small enough to pick up in VR. The bust is 48 cm tall. Downloaded by the museum's owner from Sketchfab on 2026-10-10.

object.dateLabel: c. 1345 BCE; a cast of the Berlin bust

location.name: Leiden
location.institution: Rijksmuseum van Oudheden (cast); the original is in the Neues Museum, Berlin

object.medium: Plaster cast of the painted limestone-and-stucco bust
object.description: The most famous face from the ancient world, found on 6 December 1912 on the floor of a sculptor's workshop at Amarna, the city Akhenaten built for his new religion of the sun. The workshop was Thutmose's; the bust was his model, kept on a shelf, for the queen's likeness in other works, which is why one eye was never inlaid. Painted limestone over a stucco core, 48 centimetres, 3,350 years old, and in Berlin since 1913, where Egypt has asked for it back since 1924. This is a cast of it, the Leiden museum's, released as public domain; the original has never been scanned under a free licence.
facts: The missing left eye was never finished: no trace of inlay or glue has been found in the socket.
Ludwig Borchardt, who found it, wrote 'description is useless, must be seen' in his diary that night.
CT scans in 2009 found a second, differently carved face in the limestone under the stucco.

tour: Nefertiti, carved in Thutmose's workshop at Amarna about 1345 BCE and left on a shelf when the city was abandoned. One eye was never finished.
